claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution; the components inside it inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends strategies for structuring Git repositories used to publish packages, and following them improves reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed.
Pulumi packages come in two flavors (source-based and executable-based), each versioned and released differently.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository, and its version is the Git tag on that repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow (semver Git tag, then pulumi package publish), typically performed by a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
`pulumi package publish` sends package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry.
Source-based packages referenced directly from a Pulumi.yaml file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
The version of an executable-based package is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
Cross-reference: links to packaging-components anchors #source-based-plugin-packages and #executable-based-plugin-packages, private-registry concept page, pulumi_package_publish CLI page must exist.
A repository containing multiple Pulumi packages must either release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that fights how Pulumi consumes packages.
Pulumi recommends exactly one Pulumi package per repository, regardless of package type.
Multiple components inside a single package are fine and expected; components ship together at the package's version.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
A single PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
Using a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components is technically possible, but Pulumi does not recommend it.
When unrelated components share a package, every package release versions every component the same way regardless of whether each changed, which violates semver.
Cross-reference: Publishing packages guide exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/publishing-packages/.
